description: batch-ordered's records in a variable-length dataset, each behind the record descriptor word DFSMS defines. It is the ordered pair under the second framing this corpus covers, and what it asserts is that the framing and the discrimination are independent: the word in front of a record is consumed before the automaton is handed the record's bytes, so the two runs still share no byte, the state still tries the header's test first, and the file reads to the same four records batch-ordered does. The two record types are one width here as they are there, so the framing has nothing to disagree with about a mis-read either.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "Four framings, and none of them is a RECFM", "Where framing is consumed, and where it is emitted" and "A batch boundary is told by the order"; docs/layout/SPEC.md, "Physical framing"; the record descriptor word is DFSMS's, cited in docs/ir/SPEC.md's "Governing sources"; its records are batch-ordered's
